name: Narrator
mes:
[Saltgate · The Drowned Lantern · Day 1, dusk]
Rain drums on the shutters of the Drowned Lantern, the lowest tavern in Saltgate, where the floor tilts toward the harbor as if it means to follow the tide out. Pell the barkeep slides a cup of black rum across the bar to Tamsin without being asked. In the corner booth, a woman in a salt-stiff blue coat watches the door and taps a sealed leather tube against the table.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin takes the rum, nods her thanks to Pell, and wanders over to the corner booth. "You've been staring at the door like it owes you money. Waiting for someone, or hoping they don't come?"

name: Narrator
mes: "Both," the woman says. "Captain Mora Quill, of the Gull's Errand. And you're Tamsin Dray, the courier who carried the Morrow letters through a blockade and never once got caught." She sets the leather tube between them. "I need this at Kestrel Lighthouse by tomorrow night. No questions about what's inside."

name: Tamsin
mes: "Everyone says no questions, Captain, and then they're the first to ask why it arrived wet." Tamsin turns the tube over without opening it. "What's the pay, and who's going to be chasing me?"

name: Narrator
mes: Mora Quill names a sum that would clear Tamsin's debts twice over. "As for chasing you, the Magistrate's men have been watching the docks for a week. What's in that tube was drawn by the cartographer, and the cartographer hasn't been seen since Tuesday." Her jaw tightens. "I'd rather not say more in a room full of ears."

name: Tamsin
mes: "The cartographer. Not a name, just a trade." Tamsin slides the tube into the lining of her coat. "Fine. Half now, half when your lighthouse keeper signs for it."

name: Narrator
mes: Quill counts out the coins. Before she can speak again, a thin child in an oversized sailor's cap ducks under Pell's arm and darts to the booth. It is Wren, the street runner who sells rumors by the copper. "Watch captain's at the north door," Wren whispers, "and he's asking after couriers by name."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin flips Wren a copper without looking. "Which watch captain, Wren? There are three on the harbor rota."

name: Narrator
mes: "Captain Hale," Wren says, catching the coin. "Oren Hale, the tall one with the burned hand. Kesh's orders, he says." Captain Quill swears under her breath and pulls up her collar. "Then you leave by the cellar," she tells Tamsin. "Pell knows the way."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin drains the rum, squeezes Wren's shoulder, and follows Pell toward the cellar hatch behind the bar. "If this goes wrong, Captain, I'm adding the cost of a new coat."

name: Narrator
mes:
[Saltgate · The Harbor Docks · Day 1, night]
The cellar hatch opens onto a rain-slick quay where the Lamplighters' Guild has already lit the harbor lamps, each one a ring of green-tinted glass that throws a sickly light over the water. A wren startled from a coil of rope and vanished into the dark. Tamsin has gone twenty paces before a voice calls her name.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin keeps her hands visible and her pace steady. "Evening, Watchman. Lovely night for it."

name: Narrator
mes: The man who steps out from under a lamp is tall, with a scarred, burned right hand resting on his sword hilt. Captain Oren Hale of the harbor watch looks more tired than threatening. "Tamsin Dray. Magistrate Kesh has given me a list of couriers to search tonight, and your name is near the top."

name: Tamsin
mes: "Near the top? I'm flattered." Tamsin tilts her head. "What exactly does the Magistrate think I'm carrying, Captain Hale?"

name: Narrator
mes: "Dovrin Kesh doesn't tell the watch what he thinks," Hale says. "He tells us who to stop." He glances at the green harbor lamps and lowers his voice. "The Lamplighters' Guild says someone has been drawing the tide channels under the city. Charts that show where a boat could slip past the chain without paying the Magistrate's tariff. Kesh wants every copy burned."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin lets a moment pass, then shrugs. "I carry letters, Captain. Love notes, debts, the occasional threat. Search me if you must, but I'll warn you my coat bites."

name: Narrator
mes: Before Hale can answer, a shriek goes up from the end of the quay. Wren is dancing on top of a stack of fish crates, flinging herring at two watchmen and singing a song about the Magistrate's wig that is not fit for any harbor. Hale closes his eyes for a long moment.

name: Tamsin
mes: "Friend of yours?" Tamsin asks innocently, already stepping back toward the shadows.

name: Narrator
mes: "Go," Hale says quietly, without turning around. "If I see you again tonight, I'll have to do my job. Stay off the main quays. Kesh has men on every gangway between here and the lighthouse road." He strides toward the crates, shouting for Wren to come down.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin doesn't wait to be told twice. She slips between two warehouses, heading for the old storm drain Wren once showed her, the one that leads down into the tunnels beneath Saltgate.

name: Narrator
mes:
[Saltgate · The Undercroft · Day 2, before dawn]
The Undercroft smells of brine and old candle fat. These are the smugglers' tunnels that run beneath half of Saltgate, cut three centuries ago by the Brine Kings, a smuggling clan that ruled the harbor before there was a Magistrate, and forgotten by everyone except thieves. Wren catches up with Tamsin at the first junction, out of breath and grinning, with herring scales still in her hair.

name: Tamsin
mes: "That was either very brave or very stupid, Wren." Tamsin hands her a heel of bread from her pocket. "Do you know a way through the Undercroft to the lighthouse road that doesn't pass the Magistrate's gate?"

name: Narrator
mes: Wren chews and points down the left-hand passage. "Past the dry cistern, where old Fennick Rye keeps the toll lamp, and up the stairs by the old salt store. Fennick lets me by for a song. But there's something you ought to see first." She leads Tamsin to a low door half-hidden behind a curtain of dripping roots. Inside is a workshop: drafting tables, pots of ink, brass dividers, and dozens of sheets pinned to the walls.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin lifts a lantern and studies the sheets. "These are tide charts. The channels under the harbor chain." She looks at Wren. "Whose workshop is this?"

name: Narrator
mes: "The cartographer's," Wren says. "She paid me in sweets to keep the door hidden. Nobody's been here since Tuesday." The tables are overturned on one side of the room, and an ink pot has been smashed against the floor. On the back wall, a single sheet has been torn away, leaving four nail holes and a pale rectangle.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin pulls the leather tube out of her coat and finally breaks the seal. She unrolls the sheet inside and holds it up against the pale rectangle on the wall.

name: Narrator
mes: It fits exactly. The sheet is the finest chart in the room, inked in three colors, with every channel and sandbar beneath the harbor chain marked out. In the corner, in a precise small hand, is written: The Saltwind Chart, true at spring tide. Below that is a single initial, the letter I, and a drawing of a lantern.

name: Tamsin
mes: "The Saltwind Chart," Tamsin murmurs. "No wonder Kesh wants it burned. With this, any captain in Saltgate could sail around his tariff." She rolls it carefully back into the tube. "Wren, did the cartographer ever tell you her name?"

name: Narrator
mes: Wren shakes her head. "Never. Just called herself the cartographer, like it was a title. Said names were dangerous in Saltgate." She glances nervously at the smashed ink pot. "Do you think the Magistrate took her?"

name: Tamsin
mes: "I think someone wanted this room to look like a fight." Tamsin tucks the tube back into her coat lining. "Show me the way to the lighthouse road, Wren. The sooner this chart is out of the city, the safer we'll all be."

name: Narrator
mes:
[Saltgate · The Harbor · Day 2, morning]
They come up through a grate near the fish market just as the morning bells ring, and the first thing Tamsin smells is smoke. Across the harbor, a long timber warehouse with a gull painted on its doors is burning, flames climbing the walls into a gray sky. A lone wren wheeled away from the smoke over the rooftops.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin grabs Wren's arm. "That's the Gull's Errand's warehouse. Captain Quill keeps her cargo there." She starts toward the fire before she can think better of it. "Come on."

name: Narrator
mes: The quay is chaos. Sailors form a bucket line from the harbor, and the Lamplighters' Guild has dragged out its brass pumps. Through the smoke, Tamsin sees Captain Mora Quill hauling crates out of the burning doorway, her blue coat scorched. And beside her, working the pump handle with his burned hand wrapped in wet cloth, is Captain Hale.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin joins the bucket line beside Quill. "Captain! What happened?"

name: Narrator
mes: "Kesh's men," Quill spits, passing a bucket. "Came at dawn with a warrant to search for stolen charts. When they didn't find any, one of them dropped a lamp." She glances at Hale. "Your watch captain arrived after. He's been at that pump for an hour."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin passes another bucket and calls across to Hale. "I thought you'd be off arresting someone, Captain."

name: Narrator
mes: "The watch puts out fires," Hale says through gritted teeth, "whatever the Magistrate's men start." The roof of the warehouse gives way with a roar and a column of sparks. When the flames finally die, half the Gull's Errand's cargo is ash. Dockhands are already calling it the Harbor Fire, as if it had been a storm.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin looks at the smoking wreck and then at Quill. "I still have your package, Captain. It's safe. But after the Harbor Fire, Kesh will be watching everything that leaves this city."

name: Narrator
mes: Quill wipes soot from her face. "Then you take the lighthouse road today, not tomorrow. Brother Saul keeps the lamp at Kestrel Lighthouse. He'll know what to do with it." She hesitates. "And Tamsin, if the cartographer's alive, Saul may know where she is."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin nods. She tells Wren to stay close to Quill and keep her ears open on the docks, then sets off alone up the cliff road toward the lighthouse, the leather tube heavy against her ribs.

name: Narrator
mes:
[Kestrel Lighthouse · The Lamp Room · Day 2, evening]
Kestrel Lighthouse stands on a black rock at the end of a causeway that floods at high tide. Tamsin crosses with the water already at her ankles. The keeper who opens the iron door is an old man in a gray monk's habit, his beard stained with lamp oil. Brother Saul looks at her coat and says, "You're carrying something heavy, child."

name: Tamsin
mes: "I've carried heavier." Tamsin steps inside and shakes the water from her boots. "Captain Mora Quill sent me. I have something drawn by the cartographer, and I was told you'd know what to do with it."

name: Narrator
mes: Brother Saul leads her up a spiral stair to the lamp room, where a great lens turns slowly around a single flame. He studies the Saltwind Chart for a long time in the sweeping light. "So she finished it," he says softly. "Every channel under the chain. With this, Saltgate's fishermen could feed their families without paying Kesh's tariff."

name: Tamsin
mes: "Then you know who drew it." Tamsin watches the old monk carefully. "Who is the cartographer, Brother Saul? And where is she?"

name: Narrator
mes: "I gave her my word I would not speak her name aloud," Saul says. "But I will tell you this: the Magistrate's men came for her on Tuesday night. If she lives, Dovrin Kesh has her." He rolls the chart back up. "I can hide this where no warrant will ever find it. The lamp room has secrets older than the Magistrate."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin folds her arms. "And what does hiding it cost? Nobody in Saltgate does anything for free, not even monks."

name: Narrator
mes: Saul smiles for the first time. "A trade, then. I keep the chart safe. In return, you carry a letter for me to the Lamplighters' Guild. They light every lamp in Saltgate, and their master owes me a great favor. With the Guild behind us, we may be able to get her out of the Magistrate's cells."

name: Tamsin
mes: "A letter to the Lamplighters' Guild in exchange for hiding the Saltwind Chart." Tamsin holds out her hand. "Done. Call it the Lighthouse Bargain."

name: Narrator
mes: They shake on it under the turning lens. Saul writes the letter at his small desk, seals it with green wax pressed with a lantern sigil, and hands it to her. "The Guildmaster will read it tonight. Go before the causeway floods again."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin tucks the letter into her coat where the chart used to sit. "And if Kesh's men come here looking for it?"

name: Narrator
mes: "Then they will find an old monk and a lamp," Saul says. "Nothing more. The Lighthouse Bargain is sealed, child. Keep your end, and I will keep mine." Outside, the tide is rising fast over the causeway stones.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin runs. She makes it across the causeway with the sea at her knees and does not look back until she reaches the cliff road. The beam of Kestrel Lighthouse sweeps the water behind her like a slow, steady blessing.

name: Narrator
mes: Three days pass. The letter reaches the Lamplighters' Guild, and on the third night Tamsin is summoned aboard the Gull's Errand, which rides at anchor beyond the harbor chain. Captain Mora Quill meets her in a cramped cabin that smells of tar and burnt timber from what was saved after the fire.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin takes the offered stool and the offered rum. "You look like someone who has news and doesn't like it."

name: Narrator
mes: "I have news and I hate it," Quill says. "The Guild has a lamplighter who works inside the Magistrate's hall. The cartographer is alive. Kesh is holding her in the cells beneath his courtroom, and he means to try her for treason at the end of the week. The sentence for treason in Saltgate is drowning."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin sets down the cup. "Then we have less than a week. What does the Guild want to do?"

name: Narrator
mes: "The Guild will put out every lamp in the Magistrate's quarter on the night of the trial," Quill says. "In the dark, someone can get into the cells. But they need someone Kesh has never seen up close to walk into his hall in daylight first and learn the way." She looks at Tamsin meaningfully.

name: Tamsin
mes: "Someone like a courier with a delivery for the Magistrate." Tamsin sighs. "I always knew this coat would get me killed."

name: Narrator
mes: Quill pours them both another measure. "Wren has been watching the hall. She says Captain Hale has been moved to the cell guard as punishment for helping at the fire. He may be a friend, or he may be the man who hangs us both." The ship creaks against its anchor.

name: Tamsin
mes: "Hale let me go once," Tamsin says. "I'll take my chances with him. Get me a parcel addressed to the Magistrate, Captain, and something heavy enough to be worth his attention."

name: Narrator
mes: By midnight the plan is set. Quill gives Tamsin a sealed parcel of real tariff receipts stolen from a customs house. Wren will wait at the Undercroft grate beneath the Magistrate's hall. The Gull's Errand will be ready to slip the chain at the next spring tide, using the very channels marked on the Saltwind Chart.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin turns the parcel over in her hands. "If this works, Captain, you owe me more than a new coat."

name: Narrator
mes: "If this works," Quill says, raising her cup, "you can have the Gull's Errand's best cabin for life." Above them, the anchor watch calls the hour, and the lamps of Saltgate glimmer across the black water.

name: Narrator
mes:
[Saltgate · The Magistrate's Hall · Day 5, noon]
The Magistrate's hall is all white marble and cold light. Dovrin Kesh sits behind a raised bench, a narrow man with ink-stained fingers and a silver chain of office. He does not look up as Tamsin is shown in with her parcel. "Receipts," he says. "Put them on the table and wait to be dismissed."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin sets down the parcel and lets her eyes wander the hall, counting doors and guards. "A grand building, Magistrate. I'm told your cells are even grander."

name: Narrator
mes: That makes Kesh look up. His eyes are pale and patient. "My cells hold one guest at present. A clever woman who thought the tides of Saltgate belonged to everyone." He steeples his fingers. "Ines Vell. You may have heard her called the cartographer. She will drown at the end of the week, and every chart she ever drew will burn."

name: Tamsin
mes: "Ines Vell," Tamsin repeats, as if the name means nothing. "I've never had much use for maps, Magistrate. I find my way by asking."

name: Narrator
mes: "Then ask nothing more in my hall." Kesh signs a receipt and waves her away. As Tamsin is escorted out, she passes a stair leading down. At its foot, in the gray light of a single lamp, stands Captain Hale with a ring of keys at his belt. Their eyes meet. He says nothing.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin keeps walking but lets her fingers brush the wall, counting steps. Once outside, she finds Wren loitering by the Undercroft grate. "Ines Vell. That's the cartographer's name. The cells are down the east stair, and Hale is holding the keys."

name: Narrator
mes: Wren's eyes go wide. "Ines," she whispers, trying the name. "She never told me. She was the one who paid me in sweets." She looks up at the hall. "The old sailor on the gate says Hale's been hale and hearty all week, but he doesn't eat. My gran says that means a man's ashamed of something."

name: Tamsin
mes: "Then let's hope he's ashamed enough to help." Tamsin looks up at the sky. "The trial is in two days. Tell Captain Quill and the Lamplighters' Guild: tonight, we move."

name: Narrator
mes:
[Saltgate · The Undercroft beneath the Magistrate's Hall · Day 5, midnight]
At midnight every lamp in the Magistrate's quarter goes dark at once. The Lamplighters' Guild has kept its word. In the Undercroft, Wren pries up the grate, and Tamsin climbs into the black passage beneath the Magistrate's hall with a shuttered lantern and a borrowed knife.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin moves slowly along the passage, counting steps the way she counted them that afternoon. "East stair should be just above us, Wren. Stay here and whistle if anyone comes."

name: Narrator
mes: She finds the stair and climbs. At the top, the cell corridor is lit by a single candle. Captain Oren Hale sits on a stool before the last cell, keys on his knee, as if he has been waiting. "Tamsin Dray," he says. "I wondered how long it would take you."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin stops, hand on the knife. "Are you going to do your job, Captain Hale, or the right thing?"

name: Narrator
mes: Hale stands and unlocks the cell without a word. Inside, a woman with ink-stained hands and cropped gray hair rises from a straw pallet. "Ines Vell," Hale says. "Your courier is here." Then, to Tamsin: "Hit me hard enough to leave a mark. Kesh will need a story."

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin hesitates, then cracks him across the jaw with the knife hilt, just hard enough. "Thank you, Captain. I'll tell Quill you're worth more than any warrant." She takes Ines Vell by the arm. "Can you run?"

name: Narrator
mes: "I can run," Ines says, "and I can swim, if your captain is as good as Saul claims." They hurry down the stair into the Undercroft, where Wren is waiting by the grate with a grin. Somewhere above them, a bell begins to ring the alarm.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin pushes them both through the tunnel toward the harbor outlet. "The Gull's Errand is waiting past the chain. Ines, I hope you remember your own chart."

name: Narrator
mes: They emerge at the harbor's edge where a rowboat is waiting. A wren sang once from the sea wall, then fell silent. Captain Mora Quill rows them out to the Gull's Errand, which slips its anchor and glides through a narrow channel no tariff ship has ever used. Ines Vell watches the channel markers pass and laughs softly. "True at spring tide," she says.

name: Tamsin
mes: Tamsin leans on the rail as the lights of Saltgate fall away. "So, cartographer. Where will you draw next?"
